findings.title: Owner deleted between page query and graph fetch fails the list with 500
findings.observation: the two reads are not one transaction; a concurrent delete makes the IN-fetch miss an id and the IllegalStateException becomes a 500 for the whole page.
findings.why: design chose surfacing over silently dropping: openspec/changes/paginate-sort-owners/design.md:44

findings.title: Error view hides the paginator, so a failed page cannot be retried
findings.observation: after a failed page request the table and paginator vanish; only Find Owner, back on page 0, retries.
findings.why: spec asks only an explicit error: openspec/changes/paginate-sort-owners/specs/owner-list/spec.md:130

findings.title: Prefix index may be skipped under a generic prepared-statement plan
findings.observation: LIKE ? ESCAPE with a bound value can stop using text_pattern_ops once Postgres switches to a generic plan.

findings.title: Index tests check existence, not that queries use them
findings.observation: only pg_indexes text is asserted; no EXPLAIN shows the planner picking the indexes.

findings.title: Deep page index runs a deep OFFSET plus a COUNT
findings.observation: page=107374182&size=20 passes validation and makes the database skip ~2 billion rows per call.

findings.title: Unbounded lastName length in the prefix query
findings.observation: a multi-kilobyte lastName is accepted and used in the LIKE.
findings.why: unchanged from before this change; Tomcat already caps the request line.

findings.title: Component error spec feeds a plain string, not the service's error
findings.observation: the component and the real error handler are never tested together.

findings.title: HttpParams sends "+" unencoded, read back as a space
findings.observation: claims a prefix like O+Brien reaches Spring as O Brien.
findings.why: refuted by petclinic-frontend/src/app/owners/owner.service.spec.ts:86 — + goes out as %2B, green

findings.title: Name shows "First Last" but sorts by last name
findings.observation: the order can look unsorted because the cell starts with the first name.
findings.why: sort chain decided by the human: Q&A.md:30

findings.title: Comment on #25 and Bizu notification left undone
findings.observation: task 4.4 is unchecked, so the issue still claims stale completion and "any column".
findings.why: publishing to GitHub awaits the human's approval; draft is ready.

findings.title: First/last buttons and index migration were not asked for
findings.observation: claims the four-button paginator and V4 indexes exceed the ticket.
findings.why: both in the accepted plan: openspec/changes/paginate-sort-owners/proposal.md:69 and Q&A.md:52

autofixes.title: Sort header snapped back to Name asc when the table was rebuilt
autofixes.observation: *ngIf destroys the table on a no-match search; recreated with a static matSortActive="name", the header showed Name asc while every request kept sending city,desc.
autofixes.fix: bind [matSortActive]/[matSortDirection] to the component's sort state; the new spec fails on the old template.

autofixes.title: Caller-supplied values echoed into the log on 400s
autofixes.observation: the type-mismatch handler logged the raw ?page= value and the sort message embedded the raw sort token, which the ValidationException handler logs; CRLF in either forges log lines.
autofixes.fix: log only the parameter name; the sort message no longer repeats the caller's text.

autofixes.title: Query-budget ordering assertion passed when no pets query existed
autofixes.observation: firstIndexMatching returns MAX_VALUE on no match, so "page before pets" held vacuously when no statement touched pets.
autofixes.fix: assert both the paged query and the pets query were found before comparing their order.

autofixes.title: Invalid-input test accepted any 400
autofixes.observation: only the status was checked, never the documented application/problem+json Validation Error body.
autofixes.fix: also assert the problem+json content type and the Validation Error title.

autofixes.title: Add Owner in the error state was not pinned by any test
autofixes.observation: Add Owner moved out of the table's *ngIf so it shows while loading and on error, but only the success path asserted it.
autofixes.fix: the failure spec now asserts Add Owner is still rendered.

autofixes.title: Two added lines over 119 characters
autofixes.observation: scripts/check-line-length.py refused the push: the statement-inspector property and a Cucumber step signature exceeded the 119-char limit.
autofixes.fix: split the constant string and wrap the step's function onto its own line.

assumptions.title: A non-numeric parameter is a 400 on every endpoint, not just the list
assumptions.alternative: parse page/size as strings locally; /api/owners/abc stays a 500
assumptions.why: a global handler is Spring's own default and the least code, but it changes untouched endpoints' status for malformed path ids, which nobody asked for.

assumptions.title: On a failed request, rows are cleared and the table hidden
assumptions.alternative: keep the last good page visible beneath the error
assumptions.why: stale rows under an error read as current data; but losing the paginator is what the correctness reviewer tripped on, so this is close to a coin flip.

assumptions.title: Add Owner is shown in every state, including loading and error
assumptions.alternative: show it only after the first successful load, as before
assumptions.why: the design asks for Add Owner access across loading, empty and error layouts; the old gating looked accidental rather than intended.

assumptions.title: An empty sort= or size= falls back to the default instead of a 400
assumptions.alternative: reject an empty value as malformed
assumptions.why: Spring applies defaultValue to empty strings and the spec only lists omitted parameters; nothing pins what an empty value should do.

assumptions.title: Sort tokens are exact lowercase; name,ASC is rejected
assumptions.why: the spec lists four exact tokens as the whitelist; a lenient parser would widen the contract nobody asked to widen.

assumptions.title: "Unrepresentable page" means page times size overflows the offset
assumptions.alternative: only reject a page number that overflows an int
assumptions.why: Spring Data throws a 500 when the offset exceeds an int, so that is the bound a valid request cannot cross; the int-parse overflow is caught separately.

assumptions.title: Page size documented as a 5–20 range, not an enum
assumptions.alternative: an enum of "5","10","20", typed as strings by springdoc
assumptions.why: springdoc renders allowableValues as strings on an integer, a schema lie; the exact set lives in the description instead.

assumptions.title: The service omits absent parameters; the component always sends all four
assumptions.alternative: the service fills in the defaults itself
assumptions.why: the API owns its defaults; duplicating them in the client is a second place to drift.

assumptions.title: Graph fetch without SQL DISTINCT
assumptions.why: Hibernate 6 dedupes fetch-joined roots in memory; DISTINCT only added a sort over every joined column, and the nested-data tests stay green without it.

assumptions.title: Pets cell rendered as divs, not nested table rows
assumptions.why: a <tr> in a <td> is invalid HTML the browser re-parents; no test or e2e selector depended on it.

assumptions.title: User manual text updated, screenshot left stale
assumptions.alternative: regenerate the screenshots by crawling the running UI
assumptions.why: a crawl is a separate, slow job (regen-user-manual); the text is what a reader acts on, but the picture now contradicts it.
